summary: Promote the interaction_blockers responsive-gate check (born from Test-7 negative knowledge) into the stable KINETIC evaluator. The check flags any position:fixed/absolute element covering >=50% of the viewport with pointer events enabled and (z-index>=100 OR opaque background) that is not dismissed, and fails the responsive gate when one is present. This closes a proven false-negative class: a page can pass every structural gate yet be completely unusable behind an undismissed overlay.

thresholds_met.zero_regression_evidence: yes — verified the rule FAILs the defective v-neg candidate (div.veil detected) and produces NO false positives on clean variants v0 (fixed canvas is pointer-events:none; small banner) and v2 (sticky, not an overlay).
thresholds_met.explicit_human_acceptance: NO — pending. Per doc 53, evaluator-rule promotion requires explicit human acceptance. This dry-run does NOT obtain it.

regression_tests: gates.browser.js interaction_blockers check present and active
v-neg defective candidate -> responsive gate FAIL (div.veil detected)
v0 clean candidate -> responsive gate PASS (no false positive)
v2 clean candidate -> responsive gate PASS (no false positive)

risk.compat: low — additive check inside the existing responsive gate; no API change to primitives or installer.
risk.perf: negligible — one extra getComputedStyle pass over body * during evaluation only (not at runtime).
risk.a11y: positive — catches overlays that block keyboard/pointer access to content.
risk.legal: none — no third-party assets or content involved.
